added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no baseline_suite gate log, so the store derives the added-failure count as unmeasured from the manifest's own fields (baseline_suite, after_suite) and an unmeasured count is not stored as a measured zero. The run's own gate arms, under test_logs — repair-baseline.log at cf71f7ee (3 failed) versus repair-gate-committed.log at 4481955e (0 failed) — show the repair added no failing test. An independent re-run of the six-file gate at 4481955e reproduced one failure, tests/test_crew_recover.py::test_the_follow_loop_sweeps_on_a_cadence_not_every_iteration, in a file and code path this commit does not touch; it is reported under the review's follow-ons, not folded into this count.

findings.text: follow-on: on the re-queue path, queue_dispatch selects the existing pointer before taking _pointer_lock(run_id) and then read_pointer(run_id) inside the lock; a discard that removes that pointer between the scan and the lock makes read_pointer raise 'no live run' rather than creating a fresh queued pointer, so a dispatch racing the discard of its own queued entry errors out instead of re-queueing.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the production call sites of the changed symbols: queue_dispatch at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:913, _pointer_lock under queue_dispatch at reckon/crew/runs.py:602, and the WAITING_STATES consumers that now read queued as a member — reckon/crew/recovery.py:9833, :11036, :11241, and FLEET_WAITING_STATES at :10581.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit 4481955e554616cbfb58b8cc1f8b98bf44fb911b against its base cf71f7ee54e295ef731de374354d70b84a5fb183 (the head the prior review stood for): +95/-8 across the four declared paths. recovery.py:118 adds "queued" to WAITING_STATES, runs.py:594/602 rework the dedup predicate and the pointer write, ticker.py:151/178 add the queued hue, and the test file gains three cases.
item_verdicts.done_when: §2's done-when still holds after the repair: a held local dispatch leaves one live queued pointer, no worktree, a printed run id and position, one pointer on repeat, and discard removes it. tests/test_held_dispatch_is_queued.py:12 existing cases plus the three added cases (:210 identity by section, :245 per-run lock, :254 counter) pass; the six-file gate is recorded green at 4481955e.
item_verdicts.goal: the repair closes the two defects the prior review left on run r-20261008T085254553686-a-held-dispatch-becomes-a-queued-run's queued-dispatch pointer: reckon/crew/runs.py:594 queue_dispatch now matches node.section in its identity predicate so two sections of one node no longer collapse, and reckon/crew/runs.py:602 writes the pointer under _pointer_lock(run_id) rather than only under locks/queued-dispatch.lock, so a queued write and a per-run mutation of the same pointer are mutually exclusive.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the reviewed manifest names after_suite at 4481955e (repair-gate-committed.log, 73 passed, failure_count 0) but leaves baseline_suite empty, so the store's added-failure derivation reads the base arm as absent and reports the count unmeasured; the run's own base arms sit under test_logs (repair-baseline.log at cf71f7ee, 3 failed; repair-pointer-baseline.log at cf71f7ee, 3 failed).
item_verdicts.write_paths: commit 4481955e554616cbfb58b8cc1f8b98bf44fb911b touches exactly reckon/crew/recovery.py, reckon/crew/runs.py, reckon/crew/ticker.py and tests/test_held_dispatch_is_queued.py — the four paths the delta names — and no other tracked file.

justifications.durability: the added cases fail when the fix is absent — the pointer baseline at cf71f7ee shows test_queued_identity_includes_the_section returning r-first for both sections, test_queued_write_obeys_the_per_run_pointer_lock never reaching the lock, and test_queued_counter_is_waiting_and_never_working seeing no waiting bucket — so each names a condition under which it reddens; the lock case proves exclusion with events rather than timing alone.
justifications.evidence: the repair is backed by reproduction arms and three focused tests. Caveats depress it: the reviewed manifest leaves baseline_suite empty, so the store derives the added-failure count as unmeasured from the manifest's own fields; the pointer baseline log's header names revision cf71f7ee while it collects the three tests only the head adds, so that arm's tree was not exactly cf71f7ee; and an independent re-run of the six-file gate at 4481955e reproduced one failure in tests/test_crew_recover.py that the run's own after_suite log records as passing.
justifications.fit: the repair follows the module idioms it touches: _pointer_lock and read_pointer for the pointer write, the read-modify-write shape _mutate_pointer already uses, the WAITING_STATES family for the counter, and STATE_HUE for the ticker; names are mechanism words (section, pointer lock, queued) with no plan or stage labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/runs.py:594 adds node.section to the queued-pointer identity so two held dispatches of one node in different sections of a plan from one session stay two pointers, and reckon/crew/runs.py:602 takes _pointer_lock(run_id) before writing so the queued write excludes a per-run mutation of the same file; both are the defects the prior review recorded, now closed. recovery.py:118 makes a queued run count as waiting in the fleet counter, matching §2's queued phase.
justifications.reuse: it reuses the existing per-run lock and pointer reader instead of a second lock, and extends the existing WAITING_STATES/FLEET_WAITING_STATES set rather than adding a parallel queued family, so the counter's three designed dispositions stay a partition.
justifications.scope_discipline: commit 4481955e554616cbfb58b8cc1f8b98bf44fb911b changes only the four delta paths (recovery.py, runs.py, ticker.py, tests/test_held_dispatch_is_queued.py) and no other tracked file; the new tests write only into the temporary crew home the dispatch_repo fixture sets up.
